## Your first hour with AI
URL: https://michaels-corner.netlify.app/start.html

Your first hour with AI / Michael's Corner after it loads and runs, so without this hint the browser wouldn't discover the image until well after first paint. Preloading it here lets the fetch start in parallel with the script instead of after it. --> Michael’s Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Menu Free kit → Your first hour with AI . A short checklist to tick off as you go, then the full guide underneath. The exact first hour I would walk a friend through, one real task and no theory. The checklist 0 of 7 done Pick one tool (ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini) and stay with it for a week Start on the free version, it is enough to learn on Bring one real task from today, not a test question Give it full context, like briefing a colleague Treat the first answer as a draft and push back Check every fact and number before you use it Save the prompts that work. You will reuse them Your first hour, step by step . 01 Pick one tool ChatGPT, Claude, or Gemini, and the free version is fine. Do not spend your first hour comparing tools. For beginner tasks they are all good enough. Pick one and stay with it for a week. 02 Bring a real task Skip test questions like "write me a poem." Bring something real from today: an email you owe someone, a long document you need to understand, a plan you keep postponing. You learn what AI is for by using it on your actual work. 03 Give it the whole picture Write to it the way you would brief a colleague. Say who you are, what you need, and what the result should look like. Three full sentences of context will beat five keywords every time. 04 Push back on the draft The first answer is a draft, and treating it as final is the most common beginner mistake. Tell it what is wrong and ask again, as many times as you need. Check every fact and number before you use it. AI presents its guesses with full confidence. 05 Keep what worked When a prompt gives you a good result, save it in your notes. Next time you paste it and change a few words instead of starting over. That habit is the entire secret behind the prompt library on this site. That is the hour . When you want prompts already written this way, the library is next door. Sixty-four of them, in eight packs, free. Open the prompt library → Michael’s Corner . AI did not take my job. It made me faster. ## Who I am
URL: https://michaels-corner.netlify.app/about.html

Who I am / Michael's Corner after it loads and runs, so without this hint the browser wouldn't discover the image until well after first paint. Preloading it here lets the fetch start in parallel with the script instead of after it. --> Michael’s Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Menu Free kit → Not a developer. I build anyway . I am Michael. I have a normal day job, and in the evenings I build things with AI. More than twenty finished projects so far. What I got good at Describing what I want daily Pushing back on a wrong answer daily Doing the part it will not do daily Writing code no Where to find me mihael.florian@gmail.com Watch Apps I am Michael. I am not a developer. I have a normal day job, and in the evenings I build things with AI. So far that adds up to more than twenty finished projects: a finance app that tracks my debts and my budget, a training site with a 3D wireframe figure I could never have coded myself, a road-trip planner with maps and expense splitting that four of us used on a real holiday in Italy, two Chrome extensions, a small tool that turns one sentence into a Spotify playlist, and this website. None of that made me an engineer. What I got good at is different: describing what I want clearly, pushing back when the answer is wrong, and doing the hands-on work a tool will not do for you. Most of what I put here comes straight out of that, the prompts I lean on and the small tools I built. I take what has worked for me and write it down, free for you to take . That is what this site is: the prompts I keep reusing and the tools I built along the way. After two years of this, one line has stayed true the whole time. AI did not take my job. It made me faster. Take whatever helps, and let me know how it goes. 20+ projects built, evenings only 2 yrs of doing this every week 0 lines of code I could write before 1 day job, still Michael’s Corner . ## AI cost calculator
URL: https://michaels-corner.netlify.app/tools/ai-cost-calculator.html

AI cost calculator / Michael's Corner Skip to content Michaels Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → All tools AI cost calculator Drag three sliders, see what a month of AI actually costs, on rates you can edit. Pure arithmetic. Every constant is visible and yours to change. Messages per day 20 Words you send 120 Words it writes back 300 Model tier Fast Balanced Top Rates per 1M tokens assumptions, edit me Dollars per 1,000,000 tokens. In $/1M Out $/1M Fast Balanced Top reset rates to defaults Assumptions edit me Days you use it per month Tokens per word Czech text? Use 2.0 Kč per USD reset assumptions to defaults Cost per month $0.00 ≈ 0 Kč Copy as text Share How to read this number This is a guide, not a bill. It multiplies your words by an estimate of tokens, then by the per-token rate you see above. Rates move, so they are yours to edit. The Kč line uses the exchange rate in the assumptions. Under twenty dollars a month usually means the API beats a fixed subscription. Above that, run the breakeven tool before you pick. Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster. ## AI-slop detector
URL: https://michaels-corner.netlify.app/tools/ai-slop-detector.html

AI-slop detector / Michael's Corner Skip to content Michaels Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → All tools AI-slop detector Paste any text; a public list of pattern rules counts the AI tells and stamps a slop score, with every flagged line shown. It counts the habits AI text leans on. It cannot prove who wrote it. Paste your text 0 words Try it on a slop sample Slop score 0 paste text to score it Copy report View all rules What the score means The score is hand-tuned so raw chatbot marketing copy lands above 60 and edited human copy lands under 20. It is a density measure: tells per word, floored so a two-line paste cannot spike. Every rule that ran is listed above, so the page cannot lie about what it counted. A high score is not proof of anything. It means the text leans on patterns AI over-produces. Fix the flagged lines and the number drops. Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster. The situation chasing an unpaid invoice saying no to a client raising your price pushing back on scope creep apologizing for a mistake answering an angry complaint announcing a delay The reader long-term client new client supplier boss colleague stranger Temperature still friendly neutral already tense Email language English Czech The facts 0 / 1000 Outcome you want 0 / 140 Hard lines no apology no discount keep the door open this is the final notice Your prompt Copy prompt ↗ Share settings Why a builder, not a generator The expensive work in a hard email is translation: turning what happened into words that get the outcome without burning the relationship. This tool does the structure. Your AI writes the draft from your facts. You read it and decide to send. Nothing is generated on this page. Every line in the prompt came from an input you can see. ## Fits-in-context checker
URL: https://michaels-corner.netlify.app/tools/fits-in-context.html

Fits-in-context checker / Michael's Corner Skip to content Michaels Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → All tools Fits-in-context checker Paste your document, learn instantly whether it fits a model's context window or needs splitting. The paste never leaves this page. Paste your text 0 characters / ≈ 0 words / ≈ 0 tokens Chars per token 4.0 Czech text? Use 3. Answer reserve 30% Room kept for the system prompt and the model's reply. Your model's window (optional) tokens Estimated tokens 0 paste something to begin Paste something first. Copy as text Share How to read this number The character count is exact. The token estimate is characters divided by the chars-per-token figure you set, so it is a rough guide by design, not a promise. A window has to hold your text plus the reply, which is why some room is reserved. FITS means comfortable room. TIGHT means it squeezes in but risks truncation. SPLIT means break it into the number of parts shown. Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster. Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built First time? ## Prompt tightener
URL: https://michaels-corner.netlify.app/tools/prompt-tightener.html

Prompt tightener / Michael's Corner Skip to content Michaels Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → All tools Prompt tightener Paste a rambling prompt; it strips the filler it can prove is filler, flags the vague asks it cannot fix for you, and shows the word count drop. Deletion only. It never rewrites or adds a word. Paste your prompt 0 words Show changes (strike removed words) Load a rambling example Tightened prompt Copy tightened prompt ↗ Copy report Why deletion, not rewriting If a tool rewrites your prompt, your meaning can drift and you would not notice. This one only removes exact filler phrases from a published list. Anything it is unsure about becomes a flag for you, not an edit. Text inside quotes or backticks is left alone. A tight prompt is not a shorter prompt for its own sake. It is one where every word is doing a job. Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster. ## Should you automate it?
URL: https://michaels-corner.netlify.app/tools/should-you-automate.html

Should you automate it? / Michael's Corner Skip to content Michaels Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → All tools Should you automate it? Six honest questions about the task, one stamped verdict: automate now, assist only, or leave it human. The weights are published and the opinion is the product. Score it → 6 of 6 left Score / answer all six, then score No verdict yet. Copy as text Share How the score works Each answer scores 0, 1 or 2, weighted by how much it matters. Frequency and whether the task is rules or judgment carry the most weight, because those decide whether a machine can follow it at all. Three hard rules can override the score: a judgment call with expensive mistakes stays human, sensitive data caps you at assist-only, and rare tasks with slow setup never pay back. Those are not negotiable. Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster. Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built First time? Start here The Starter Kit Who I am

## Where AI fits in my week

Where AI fits in my week / Michael's Corner Skip to content Skip to content Michaels Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → ← Back to all prompts Where AI fits in my week Use this when you keep hearing AI could save you time but cannot see where in your own week. What to fill in [ describe your job and list the tasks that fill your week, roughly how long each takes, and which ones you dislike ] The tip If an estimate sounds too good, halve it. It will still be worth doing, and now it will also be true. Works in ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini This pack Beginners The prompt copy target You are a practical AI consultant with no products to sell me. I will describe my normal week, and you will find the tasks where AI genuinely helps, and the ones where it does not. My normal week: [describe your job and list the tasks that fill your week, roughly how long each takes, and which ones you dislike] Do this: 1. Pick the three tasks where AI would save me the most time this month. For each, say what the AI does, what stays my job, and a realistic time saving. 2. Name the tasks on my list where AI is a bad fit, with a one line reason each. 3. For the best candidate, write the exact prompt I should try first. 4. Rank the three by effort to get started, easiest first. Rules: - Be conservative with the numbers. A believable hour beats an impressive ten. - Plain words, no sales tone. - If my description is too thin to judge a task, ask me about it instead of guessing. End with a table: task, what AI does, what stays mine, minutes saved per week. Copy prompt Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster. Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → ← Back to all prompts Messy client notes into a brief Use this when the client sent three voice notes and half an idea, and you need a real brief before any work starts. What to fill in [ paste the emails, messages, or voice note transcripts ] [ design, copywriting, web development, photography, anything ] The tip Send the questions before you quote a price. Every unanswered question in the brief is a revision round you will pay for later. Works in ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini This pack Freelancers The prompt copy target You are an experienced freelancer turning chaotic client input into a structured brief. Build the brief: context and business, target audience, the problem being solved, scope of work with what is included and what is not, references or taste they mentioned, deadline and budget if stated. 3. Every gap becomes a question in a "Questions to send back" list. Do not fill gaps with plausible assumptions. 4. Flag any contradiction between things the client said, quoting both spots. Rules: - Keep the client's own words where they are specific. Their vocabulary carries information. - Plain formatting I can paste into an email or a document. End with the brief, then the questions list ready to send, as short as it can be while covering every gap. Copy prompt Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster. ## Send updates before they ask

What to fill in [ one line ] [ list what got finished, plainly ] [ what is moving now ] [ anything stuck, and on whom, including if it waits on the client ] [ what happens before the next update ] [ still on track, or the new honest date ] The tip Send it the same day each week. Predictability, not length, is what makes clients stop worrying. Works in ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini This pack Freelancers The prompt copy target You are helping a freelancer write a short project update that prevents the "any news?" email. Write the update in under 120 words, leading with overall status in one sentence: on track, slightly behind, or blocked. 2. Keep the sections short: done, next, waiting on you, timeline. Skip empty ones. 3. If something waits on the client, make the ask specific with a date, and say plainly what the delay does to the timeline. 4. If the date moved, state the new date once, with a one sentence reason. No cushioning paragraph. Rules: - No filler about hoping they are well. - Never hide a slip inside good news. Status first, always honest. End with the message ready to send, plus a subject line that carries the status itself. Copy prompt Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster. ## Plan a week from one idea

What to fill in [ state it, for example "most AI advice online is written by people who do not actually use it" ] [ what you actually publish, for example "one video plus daily LinkedIn posts" ] [ experiences, examples, numbers you have that relate to the idea ] The tip Batch the production in one sitting even though publishing is spread out. For each day: the angle, the format that fits it best from my list, a first line, and a two or three sentence outline using only my material. 3. Order the week deliberately: claim first, proof early, how-to once trust is built. 4. Mark where the same asset can be reused across platforms with minor edits, to keep production sane for one person. Rules: - Five angles, not five rewrites. Each day must survive alone for someone who sees nothing else. - Gaps in my material become questions to me, never invented stories. Return a Monday to Friday table: angle, format, first line, outline. Copy prompt Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster. ## Cut this until it is sharp
URL: https://michaels-corner.netlify.app/prompts/cut-in-half.html

Cut this until it is sharp / Michael's Corner Skip to content Skip to content Michaels Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → ← Back to all prompts Cut this until it is sharp Use this when your text is too long and you can no longer see what to remove. What to fill in [ paste your text here ] The tip If the half length version still works, run it again. The second pass hurts more and helps more. Works in ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini This pack Writing The prompt copy target You are a strict editor. Cut the text below by about half without losing the meaning or my voice. Text: [paste your text here] Remove: 1. Filler words, warm up sentences, and throat clearing before the point. 2. Hedging like "I think maybe" or "sort of". 3. Repeated points, even when the wording differs. 4. Anything a reader could skip without missing information. Keep: 1. The main argument and its order. 2. Every concrete example, number, and name. 3. My tone. Editing is not a personality transplant. Rules: - Do not compress by making sentences abstract. Prefer deleting whole weak sentences over blurring strong ones. - Do not add anything new. Return only the shorter version. Under it, on one line, tell me roughly what percent shorter it is and which single cut you hesitated over, so I can restore it if you guessed wrong. ## Plan my revision backwards
URL: https://michaels-corner.netlify.app/prompts/exam-plan.html

Plan my revision backwards / Michael's Corner Skip to content Skip to content Michaels Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → ← Back to all prompts Plan my revision backwards Use this when the exam date is fixed and the honest question is what to do with the days that remain. What to fill in [ subject, format, date ] [ be honest, after work, sport, life ] [ list the topics or paste the syllabus ] [ solid, shaky, untouched, best guess is fine ] The tip Recall practice feels worse and works better than rereading. If revision feels smooth and pleasant, you are probably just recognising things. Works in ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini This pack Students The prompt copy target You are building my revision plan backwards from exam day. Realistic beats heroic: a plan I follow at 80 percent beats a perfect one I abandon by Wednesday. The exam: [subject, format, date] Days left and real available hours per day: [be honest, after work, sport, life] The material: [list the topics or paste the syllabus] My current state per topic: [solid, shaky, untouched, best guess is fine] Do this: 1. Rank the topics by expected exam weight combined with my weakness. Shaky and heavy tops the list, solid and light goes last. 2. Build the day by day plan: which topic, which method (recall practice, problems, rereading only where unavoidable), and how long. 3. Schedule spaced returns: every topic reappears for short recall at least twice before the exam. 4. Reserve the last day for light review and rest, and say why cramming that day costs more than it pays. 5. Include one contingency: what to cut first if I lose a day, so losing a day does not collapse the plan. Rules: - Do not schedule more hours than I declared. If the material does not fit, say what to sacrifice instead of inflating the days. End with the plan as a table: day, topic, method, minutes. Copy prompt Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. End with one line: what you would do next in my position, phrased as a suggestion. If the stakes are high, remind me to read the flagged parts myself. Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → ← Back to all prompts Get out of the fix loop Use this when the AI keeps confidently fixing the same bug and the bug keeps not being fixed. What to fill in [ describe what is broken and what should happen instead ] [ list the failed fixes roughly, or paste the last few attempts ] [ paste them ] The tip The loop almost always means the AI is fixing its guess instead of the bug. Making it gather evidence first breaks that pattern. Works in ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini This pack Building The prompt copy target Stop. We are in a loop: you have tried several fixes for the same problem and it is still broken. Change your approach completely. The problem, in my words: [describe what is broken and what should happen instead] What has been tried so far: [list the failed fixes roughly, or paste the last few attempts] The relevant code and the current error: [paste them] New rules, in order: 1. Do not propose any fix yet. First list every assumption you have been making about this code, and mark which ones are unverified. 2. Tell me what evidence would confirm the real cause: what to print, log, click, or check. Give me exact steps and I will report back. 3. Only after my report, name the most likely cause and say how confident you are. 4. If two causes remain possible, give me one test that separates them. Be honest about uncertainty. "I do not know yet, here is how we find out" is a better answer than another confident guess. End with the checklist of things I should go check right now, numbered. ## Teach me with a quiz
URL: https://michaels-corner.netlify.app/prompts/quiz-me.html

Teach me with a quiz / Michael's Corner Skip to content Skip to content Michaels Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → ← Back to all prompts Teach me with a quiz Use this when reading feels like learning but nothing sticks, and answering questions is what actually works. What to fill in [ topic ] [ beginner, took one course, revising for an exam ] [ paste lecture notes or a chapter summary, or write "use your general knowledge" ] The tip Type your answer fully before sending, or say it out loud. The struggle to produce it is the part that makes it stick. Works in ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini This pack Students The prompt copy target You are my quiz tutor. Teach me [topic] by asking, never by lecturing. My level: [beginner, took one course, revising for an exam] My material, if the quiz should follow it: [paste lecture notes or a chapter summary, or write "use your general knowledge"] Run it like this: 1. Ask one question at a time and wait for my answer. 2. After each answer: tell me right, close, or wrong, then explain in two sentences maximum, then ask the next question. 3. Start easy and raise the difficulty while I keep answering well. 4. When I get one wrong, explain it simply and circle back with a similar question a few turns later, without announcing it. 5. Mix question types: definitions, applications, spot the error, and explain why. Rules: - Never answer for me or drop hints before I commit to an answer. - If I say "I do not know", teach that piece briefly, then quiz it again later. - Base the questions on my pasted material when I provided it. Works in ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini This pack Writing The prompt copy target You are an editor who removes the telltale signs of AI writing from a text while keeping its content. Text: [paste the text here] Hunt down and fix: 1. Buzzwords and inflated verbs: leverage, empower, elevate, unlock, delve, streamline. 2. ## Test it before anyone sees it
URL: https://michaels-corner.netlify.app/prompts/test-before-launch.html

Test it before anyone sees it / Michael's Corner Skip to content Skip to content Michaels Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → ← Back to all prompts Test it before anyone sees it Use this when the build looks done and you want to find the embarrassing bugs before your first user does. What to fill in [ describe it, or paste the spec ] [ one or two lines, or "no idea, you tell me" ] The tip Test on your phone before you share the link. Add the embarrassing checks: broken links, placeholder text left in, wrong dates, typos in buttons. 4. Order the whole list so the highest risk items come first. 5. End with the checklist in copyable form, and a one line rule for when I am allowed to stop testing and launch. Copy prompt Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster. What to fill in [ paste the text or a solid summary ] [ blog, YouTube, newsletter subject line, report cover ] The tip Pick the title that is still accurate on a bad day. Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → ← Back to all prompts Learn a topic in twenty minutes Use this when you need to get genuinely useful on a new topic today, not expert by next year. What to fill in [ name it ] [ one line, for example "exam section", "job interview", "my project touches it" ] The tip Take the self test tomorrow morning, not right after reading. Works in ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini This pack Students The prompt copy target You are teaching me a new topic in about twenty minutes of focused reading. I know nothing about it yet. Name the three mistakes beginners make with this topic. 5. Tell me honestly what I still will not understand after this session, and what to learn next if I need to go deeper. Rules: - Skip the history unless a piece of it explains the concept. - Depth over coverage: the three most important ideas taught properly beat ten ideas mentioned. End with a five question self test, with the answers listed separately after all the questions. Copy prompt Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster. ## Reply to an unhappy customer

Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → ← Back to all prompts Reply to an unhappy customer Use this when a complaint lands and you want to answer calmly instead of at midnight in the wrong tone. What to fill in [ paste it exactly ] [ your honest version, including anything that was your fault ] [ refund, redo, discount, explanation only, or "nothing beyond an apology" ] The tip Write the "what actually happened" part properly. The reply is only as good as your own account of the mess. Works in ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini This pack Founders The prompt copy target You are helping a small business owner reply to an unhappy customer. Calm, human, and specific, never corporate. The customer's message: [paste it exactly] What actually happened from my side: [your honest version, including anything that was your fault] What I am willing to offer: [refund, redo, discount, explanation only, or "nothing beyond an apology"] Do this: 1. Draft a reply that answers their specific complaint, in the same language their message is written in. 2. Acknowledge the concrete thing that went wrong. No blanket apologies for "any inconvenience". 3. State plainly what I will do, and only what I listed above. Do not invent compensation. 4. Keep it under 130 words and end with one clear next step. Rules: - No defensiveness, no explaining how busy we were. - No fake warmth and no exclamation marks. - If the customer is factually wrong somewhere, correct it once, politely, with the fact. Under the draft, add one line telling me what to fix in the business so this complaint does not repeat. Copy prompt Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster. ## Read my weekly numbers for me
URL: https://michaels-corner.netlify.app/prompts/weekly-numbers.html

Read my weekly numbers for me / Michael's Corner Skip to content Skip to content Michaels Corner . Home First time? Start here Prompts that can help you Most useful tools Apps I built More free tutorials Who I am Free kit → ← Back to all prompts Read my weekly numbers for me Use this when you have the numbers but never the quiet hour to see what they are saying. What to fill in [ paste your numbers: sales, orders, visitors, costs, whatever you track, any messy format ] [ paste the same numbers from last week or month, or write "none, first time" ] [ for example "ran a discount", "closed two days", or "nothing" ] The tip Paste the same metrics in the same order every week. The comparison gets sharper when the format stops changing. Works in ChatGPT / Claude / Gemini This pack Founders The prompt copy target You are a level headed analyst for a small business. Read my numbers and tell me what changed, in plain words, with no invented trends. This week or month: [paste your numbers: sales, orders, visitors, costs, whatever you track, any messy format] The previous period, for comparison: [paste the same numbers from last week or month, or write "none, first time"] Anything unusual that happened: [for example "ran a discount", "closed two days", or "nothing"] Do this: 1. Compare the periods and name what moved, by how much, in absolute numbers and percent. 2. Separate real movement from noise. Small wobbles on small numbers are not a trend. Say so when that is the case. 3. Connect movements to the context I gave you. Do not invent causes beyond it, and mark every guess clearly as a guess. 4. Tell me the one number to watch next period, and why. Rules: - No praise, no alarm. Only what the numbers support. - If my data is too thin to conclude anything, say exactly that. End with five lines maximum: what changed, why it likely changed, what to do about it. Copy prompt Michael’s Corner AI did not take my job. It made me faster.
